newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore manufacturing output falls in third qtr.
newsitem.headline: Singapore manufacturing output falls in third qtr.

text.p: Singapore confirmed on Friday just how badly its economy had been hit by the worldwide slowdown in demand for electronics products.

Detailing economic growth figures announced earlier in the week, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said the city-state's gross domestic product (GDP) grew just 3.2 percent year-on-year in the third quarter of 1996, compared with 7.5 percent in the second quarter and 11.4 percent in the first.

The ministry repeated the forecast made by Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong on Tuesday that the country's growth would be about six percent for 1996 as a whole, and average between five and seven percent in 1997.
Inflation, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), would average below 2.0 percent year-on-year in 1996 and stay on the same low trend next year, the ministry said.
It said the main reason for the slower growth in the third quarter was a fall in manufacturing output, which declined by 4.3 percent after growing by 6.5 percent in the second quarter.
The economic slowdown follows a slump in global demand for electronics products, on which the island is heavily dependent.
Electronics, computers and related products account for about 45 percent of Singapore's manufacturing output and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.

Singapore's labour productivity fell 2.8 percent year-on-year in the third quarter after growing one percent in the second quarter. The ministry had previously said labour productivity grew 4.2 percent in the first quarter of the year.
"There are some very worrying numbers here," said Desmond Supple, senior emerging markets economist at Independent Economic Analysis in Singapore.
"If the economy slows, productivity would be expected to decline, but the severity of the fall-off is very worrying," he said. "It shouldn't be as severe as this."
